title: Management Practices and Practice Guides

header.html: Define management practice; know the two practice groups (general, and product and service management); understand the role of the practices within the ITIL Value System; explain the structure and the benefits of the ITIL Practice Guides; define metric and critical success factor
the official ITIL Foundation (Version 5) syllabus, version 5.0 (February 2026), category 4.5

toc.title: Role of the practices in the Value System

html:
1What a management practice is

A management practice is a set of organizational resources designed for performing work or accomplishing an objective. It combines people, processes, information and technology, and partners (the four dimensions).

ITIL describes 34 management practices. They are organized into two groups:

Group What it covers Examples
General management practices Practices adopted from general business and used across the organization strategy management, risk management, information security management
Product and service management practices Practices developed for product and service management incident management, problem management, change enablement, service desk

Old wording ITIL 4 had three groups: general, service and technical management practices. Version 5 uses two. [Verify live]

Exam tip

. Two groups: general, and product and service. If an option lists "general, service and technical", it is the old wording.

2Role of the practices in the Value System

The practices are the third working element the value chain activities draw on: each activity uses one or more practices, and a practice can contribute to several activities. The practices turn guiding principles and governance into repeatable work.

3The ITIL Practice Guides

Each practice is described in an ITIL Practice Guide that gives practical guidance. Typically a guide covers (in plain words):

Part Content
Purpose and key terms What the practice is for, and its vocabulary
Scope and value What it covers, and the value it brings
Processes and activities The work done inside the practice
Four dimensions Organizations and people, information and technology, partners and suppliers, value streams
Success factors and metrics How to tell the practice is working

Benefits: the guides give a consistent structure, reusable good practice, and a common language across teams. [Verify live]

4Metric and critical success factor

Term Meaning
Metric A measurement or calculation that is monitored and reported to show how well something performs
Critical success factor (CSF) A necessary precondition for success: something that must happen for an outcome to be achieved
Exam tip

. A CSF says what must be true. A metric says how you measure it.

Exam tip

. Two groups in Version 5: general and product and service management. An option with three groups (general, service, technical) is the ITIL 4 wording.

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Which statement about management practices in Version 5 is CORRECT? (1) They are organized into two groups. (2) One group is general management practices. (3) They are organized into general, service and technical groups. (4) There are only five of them.

  • A3 and 4
  • B1 and 2
  • C1 and 4
  • D2 and 3
Show the answer

Answer: B. Two groups, one of which is general.

S2Incident management belongs to which practice group?

  • AProduct and service management practices
  • BGeneral management practices
  • CFinancial practices
  • DGovernance practices
Show the answer

Answer: A. Incident management is developed for product and service management.

S3A team asks which target must be true for a project to succeed. Which term describes it?

  • AMetric
  • BCritical success factor
  • CKnown error
  • DOutput
Show the answer

Answer: B. A CSF is a necessary precondition for success.

S4Identify the missing word(s). A [ ? ] is a set of organizational resources designed for performing work or accomplishing an objective.

  • AService offering
  • BProduct prototype
  • CManagement practice
  • DOperating model
Show the answer

Answer: C. That is the definition of a management practice.

S5What is the main benefit of the ITIL Practice Guides?

  • AThey replace the guiding principles
  • BThey guarantee a pass mark
  • CThey set a company's strategy
  • DThey give a consistent, practical structure for each practice
Show the answer

Answer: D. They offer consistent, reusable guidance.

S6A manager reports the percentage of incidents resolved within the agreed time. What is this?

  • AA critical success factor
  • BA prototype
  • CA metric
  • DA service level agreement
Show the answer

Answer: C. A measurement monitored and reported is a metric.

5.2 Recall questions

R1Define a management practice.

Show the answer

A set of organizational resources designed for performing work or accomplishing an objective.

R2How many practice groups are there in Version 5?

Show the answer

Two.

R3Name them.

Show the answer

General management practices, and product and service management practices.

R4How many practices does ITIL describe?

Show the answer

34.

R5Define a critical success factor.

Show the answer

A necessary precondition for success.

R6What is a metric?

Show the answer

A measurement or calculation that is monitored and reported.
